claims.text: The brittle window between 550°C and 750°C is driven by a critical threshold of L1₂ chemical ordering.
Increasing L1₂ ordering in the FCC matrix increases the antiphase-boundary energy.
Peak L1₂ ordering minimizes the intrinsic stacking-fault energy in the FCC matrix.
High antiphase-boundary energy restricts the dissociation width of Shockley partial dislocations.
High antiphase-boundary energy inhibits dislocation cross-slip.
Suppression of cross-slip forces dislocations to move by planar slip.
Planar slip localizes stress at serrations of jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
Stress localization at jagged B2/FCC interfaces causes premature crack nucleation and brittleness.
Aging near 750°C decreases the L1₂ long-range-order parameter.
Reduced L1₂ order lowers antiphase-boundary energy, restores cross-slip, and recovers ductility.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 is ductile.
The as-cast alloy consists of an FCC matrix and B2 precipitates.
The as-cast B2/FCC phase boundaries are smooth.
Aging at 600°C produces peak L1₂ ordering with local chemistry near the stoichiometric Ni3Al ratio.
Aging at 750°C produces partial disordering relative to the 600°C state.
Aging in the brittle regime creates jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Elongation reaches a minimum near 600°C and recovers near 750°C.
The ductile high-temperature-aged state has smoother B2/FCC boundaries or ductile transition zones along the phase boundaries.
The brittle-to-ductile transition occurs when the L1₂ order parameter falls below a threshold associated with the antiphase-boundary energy exceeding the critical stress for cross-slip.
SAED superlattice-spot intensity can be used to quantify the L1₂ order parameter for the proposed comparison.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis places reversal at temperatures greater than 750°C, whereas the intervention and predicted outcome assign partial disordering and recovered ductility at 750°C, and the stated experimental range ends at 750°C.

The boundary compares APBE, an energy per unit area, directly with a critical stress for cross-slip. These are not directly comparable quantities without an explicit activation model converting APBE into a critical stress.
